VAL-098 bitwise-reproduced fixed-denominator audit on five Stanford and six Matterport pairs; current accuracy rejects promotion
VAL-099 bitwise-reproduced confidence selectivity audit; ranking is monotonic on eleven pairs but high-accuracy subsets cover only about fourteen percent of the fixed population

VAL-100 absolute-threshold transfer audit; only six of eleven within-domain and four of eleven all-other-pair folds pass, while Matterport-to-Stanford cross-domain calibration fails, so the original score is not portable or calibrated

BUG-101 separates face taper from matching confidence without changing any non-confidence output on eleven public pairs; top-quartile ranking improves, but corrected absolute-threshold transfer still passes only four of eleven leave-one-out folds and one of two domain directions

VAL-108 freezes three two-source references per public domain before inference; multibaseline aggregation improves fixed-population accuracy in five of six triplets, but gross outliers remain high and strict source-label consensus retains only about four percent of Stanford and ten percent of Matterport observable support

VAL-109 replays parallax-weighted mean on the unchanged public triplets; it underperforms the existing two-source lower median in both domains, so no default changes and occlusion-aware source selection remains open

VAL-110 applies a frozen parameter-free source-consensus factor to the existing confidence without changing range or validity; top-quartile accuracy falls slightly in both domains and absolute-threshold transfer pass counts do not improve, so the runtime score remains unchanged

VAL-111 freezes a two-pass per-pixel source-group selection from complete unary cost curves; it reduces Stanford gross outliers but lowers coverage and fixed-population accuracy in both domains and worsens Matterport gross outliers, so the policy is rejected and not exposed

VAL-112 prospectively freezes three registered sources for three references per public domain; the true three-source median reduces gross label outliers in both domains but loses coverage and does not improve overall fixed-population accuracy, leaving source-count-portable cost normalization and acceptance open

VAL-113 freezes five acceptance-gate policies on the unchanged public three-source sets; the absolute cost gate changes no result, confidence explains only part of the source-count coverage loss, and texture controls absolute coverage without causing the regression, so no runtime default changes

API-114 adds cumulative face-pixel acceptance diagnostics without changing any of 24 frozen public output-array hashes; boundary hypotheses dominate the Stanford two-to-three-source loss and confidence dominates the Matterport loss

VAL-115 prospectively tests discrete acceptance of endpoint labels; coverage rises but fixed accuracy falls slightly and conditional gross error regresses beyond the frozen tolerance in both domains, so the candidate option is removed

VAL-116 freezes twelve new view-disjoint public pairs before inference; report-only confidence improves coverage and fixed-population accuracy in both domains but exceeds the Stanford conditional-gross tolerance, so the candidate option is removed and the threshold default remains

VAL-117 freezes twelve further view-disjoint public pairs before inference and changes only the unary cost; AD-Census improves fixed-population accuracy in both domains, passes coverage, gross-error and runtime gates, and reproduces all 24 payload hashes exactly, making it the candidate default pending independent review

VAL-119 reuses the already observed VAL-098 development pairs in a controlled 512x1024 factorial; doubling the range lattice gives a modest domain-uneven gain, while doubling face resolution with unchanged pixel windows lowers fixed accuracy in both domains, exposing angular support invariance as a promotion blocker

API-120 separates ERP-feature and face-cost tap spacing in degrees while preserving the omitted-option path byte-identically; the combined angular route improves fixed-population accuracy by about 0.11 in both development domains and reproduces all eleven candidate payload hashes exactly

VAL-121 freezes twelve new view-disjoint pairs before inference; after prediction-independent exclusion of sky/no-return and fixed observability masking, angular ERP and face support improves coverage, fixed delta<1.25 and conditional >2x error in both domains, stays below 1.35x median runtime, and exactly reproduces the evidence file plus all 24 payload and population hashes
REV-122 independently reproduces the complete VAL-121 evidence SHA plus all 24 output and population hashes and approves angular support for default integration

REV-123 independently reproduces all VAL-117 payloads, populations, metrics and aggregates; its only raw evidence difference is the additive post-VAL-117 angular-neighbourhood diagnostic, and removing only that field reconstructs the original evidence SHA exactly
API-124 integrates reviewed AD-Census and angular-support defaults for new Experimental option objects while explicit legacy values and older saved configurations retain historical behavior
